sentences.ar: אָדָם אֶחָד, עָשִׁיר בְּזָהָב וּבְמִקְנֶה וּבְקַרְקָעוֹת, הָיָה מִתְגָּאֶה בְּעָשְׁרוֹ וְהָיָה קוֹרֵא עַל עַצְמוֹ: "בְּצֵל הַכֶּסֶף – בְּצֵל הַחָכְמָה".
sentences.en: A certain man, rich in gold, in cattle, and in land, used to boast of his wealth, and he would say of himself: "In the shelter of money is the shelter of wisdom."

sentences.ar: נָפְלָה בְּאוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם מַגֵּפָה וְכָל הַשְּׁוָרִים מֵתוּ בַּמַּגֵּפָה.
sentences.en: A plague broke out in that place, and all the oxen died in the plague.

sentences.ar: וּכְשֶׁנֶּעְצְרָה הַמַּגֵּפָה לֹא הָיוּ לוֹ שְׁוָרִים לַחֲרֹשׁ אֶת שְׂדוֹתָיו, עַד שֶׁהֶעֱלוּ קוֹצִים וְדַרְדָרִים.
sentences.en: And when the plague stopped, he had no oxen to plow his fields, so that they grew thorns and thistles.

sentences.ar: מֶה עָשָׂה אוֹתוֹ אִישׁ?
sentences.en: What did that man do?

sentences.ar: נָטַל אַרְנָק שֶׁל דִינָרִים, לֹא פָּחוֹת מִמֵּאָה, וְהָלַךְ לִכְפָר רָחוֹק אֶחָד, שֶׁהָיָה מְשֻׁפָּע בִּבְהֵמוֹת מְשֻׁבָּחוֹת, לִקְנוֹת שְׁוָרִים לַחֲרֹשׁ קַרְקְעוֹתָיו.
sentences.en: He took a purse of dinars, no fewer than a hundred, and went to a distant village that had plenty of fine animals, to buy oxen to plow his land.

sentences.ar: בַּדֶּרֶךְ פְּגָשׁוֹ אֵלִיָּהוּ זָכוּר לַטּוֹב בִּדְמוּת זָקֵן עוֹבֵר־אֹרַח.
sentences.en: On the way, Elijah, of blessed memory, met him in the guise of an old wayfarer.

sentences.ar: אַָמַר לוֹ: לְהֵיכָן אַתָּה הוֹלֵךְ, בְּנִי?
sentences.en: He said to him: "Where are you going, my son?"

sentences.ar: עָנָה: לִכְפָר פְּלוֹנִי לִקְנוֹת שְׁוָרִים לַחֲרִישָׁה.
sentences.en: He answered: "To such-and-such a village to buy oxen for plowing."

sentences.ar: אַָמַר לוֹ: אֱמֹר, בְּנִי: אִם יִרְצֶה הַשֵּׁם.
sentences.en: He said to him: "Say, my son: God willing."

sentences.ar: זַָקַף חָטְמוֹ כְּנֶגְדוֹ וְאָמַר: אִם יִרְצֶה וְאִם לֹא יִרְצֶה – הֲרֵי מְעוֹתַי בְּיָדִי וְאֶעֱשֶׂה רְצוֹנִי.
sentences.en: He turned up his nose at him and said: "Whether He wills it or not — my money is in my hand and I will do as I please."

sentences.ar: אָמַר לוֹ הַזָּקֵן: וְלֹא בְּהַצְלָחָה.
sentences.en: The old man said to him: "And not with success."

sentences.ar: הָלַךְ בְּאוֹתוֹ דֶרֶךְ וְנָפַל הָאַרְנָק וְלֹא הִרְגִישׁ.
sentences.en: He went on that road, and the purse fell without his noticing.

sentences.ar: כְּשֶׁבָּא לַכְּפָר הֶרְאוּהוּ עֲשֶׂרֶת צִמְדֵי בָּקָר תַּאֲוָה לָעֵינַיִם.
sentences.en: When he came to the village, they showed him ten pairs of oxen, a delight to the eyes.

sentences.ar: שָׁלַח יָדוֹ לָקַחַת אֶת הָאַרְנָק וְלֹא מְצָאוֹ.
sentences.en: He reached for the purse to take it, and did not find it.

sentences.ar: מִיָּד חָזַר לְבֵיתוֹ וְנָטַל מָמוֹן אַחֵר (שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ הַרְבֵּה) וְהָלַךְ לַכְּפָר בְּדֶרֶךְ אַחֶרֶת, שֶׁלֹא יִפְגַע בּוֹ אוֹתוֹ זָקֵן.
sentences.en: He immediately returned to his house and took other money (of which he had much) and went to the village by another road, so that the old man would not meet him.

sentences.ar: נִזְדַּמֵּן לוֹ הַמְבַשֵּׂר בִּדְמוּת זָקֵן אַחֵר.
sentences.en: The herald came upon him in the guise of another old man.

sentences.ar: אָמַר לוֹ: לְהֵיכָן אַתָּה הוֹלֵךְ, בְּנִי?
sentences.en: He said to him: "Where are you going, my son?"

sentences.ar: עָנָה: לִקְנוֹת שְׁוָרִים.
sentences.en: He answered: "To buy oxen."

sentences.ar: אַָמַר לוֹ: וְאֵינְךָ אוֹמֵר: אִם יִרְצֶה הַשֵּׁם?
sentences.en: He said to him: "And won't you say: God willing?"

sentences.ar: עִקֵּם חָטְמוֹ כְּנֶגְדוֹ וְאָמַר: אִם יִרְצֶה וְאִם לֹא יִרְצֶה – הֲרֵי דִינָרַי בְּאַרְנָקִי וְאֵינִי חֹושֵׁשׁ לְשׁוּם דָבָר.
sentences.en: He twisted up his nose at him and said: "Whether He wills it or not — my dinars are in my purse and I fear nothing."

sentences.ar: הָלַךְ הָאִישׁ לְדַרְכּוֹ.
sentences.en: The man went on his way.

sentences.ar: נָפְלָה עָלָיו שֵׁנָה וְשָׁכַב בִּמְצָרוֹ שֶׁל שָׂדֶה.
sentences.en: Sleep fell upon him, and he lay down at the edge of a field.

sentences.ar: בָּא אֵלִיָּהוּ וְשָׁמַט מִתַּחְתָּיו אֶת הָאַרְנָק וְנֶעְלַם.
sentences.en: Elijah came, slipped the purse out from under him, and disappeared.

sentences.ar: כְּשֶׁהֵקִיץ מִשְּׁנָתוֹ לֹא מָצָא כְּלוּם.
sentences.en: When he woke from his sleep, he found nothing.

sentences.ar: חָזַר לְבֵיתוֹ בְּנֶפֶשׁ זוֹעֶפֶת, נָטַל מָמוֹן שְׁלִישִׁי וְהָלַךְ בַּדֶּרֶךְ הָרִאשׁוֹנָה.
sentences.en: He returned to his house with a raging soul, took a third sum of money, and went by the first road.

sentences.ar: בָּא אֵלָיו אֵלִיָּהוּ זָכוּר לַטּוֹב וְאָמַר לוֹ: לְהֵיכָן אַתָּה הוֹלֵךְ, בְּנִי?
sentences.en: Elijah, of blessed memory, came to him and said to him: "Where are you going, my son?"

sentences.ar: אָמַר: לִכְפַָר פְּלוֹנִי לִקְנוֹת שְׁוָרִים, אִם יִרְצֶה הַשֵּׁם.
sentences.en: He said: "To such-and-such a village to buy oxen, God willing."

sentences.ar: אָמַר לוֹ הַזָּקֵן: לֵךְ לְשָׁלוֹם וּבְהַצְלָחָה.
sentences.en: The old man said to him: "Go in peace and with success."

sentences.ar: בְּאוֹתוֹ רֶגַע הֶחֱזִיר אֵלִיּהוּ מָאתַיִם דִינָרָיו לְתוֹךְ אַרְנָקוֹ, וְהוּא לֹא רָאָה וְלֹא יָדַע.
sentences.en: At that moment Elijah put his two hundred dinars back into his purse, and the man neither saw it nor knew it.

sentences.ar: כְּשֶׁבָּא לַכְּפָר הֶרְאוּהוּ עֲשֶׂרֶת צִמְדֵי בָּקָר יָפִים מִן הָרִאשׁוֹנִים.
sentences.en: When he came to the village, they showed him ten pairs of oxen, finer than the first ones.

sentences.ar: קָפַץ עָלָיו חִשְׁקוֹ לִקְנוֹתָם.
sentences.en: A desire to buy them leaped upon him.

sentences.ar: אָמַר לְבַעֲלֵיהֶם: בְּכַמָּה?
sentences.en: He said to their owners: "For how much?"

sentences.ar: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: בְּמֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים דִינָרִים.
sentences.en: They said to him: "For a hundred and twenty dinars."

sentences.ar: אָמַר: כַּמָּה אֲנִי מִצְטַעֵר, שֶׁאֵין עִמִּי אֶלָּא מֵאָה דִינָרִים בִּלְבָד.
sentences.en: He said: "How sorry I am that I have with me only a hundred dinars and no more."

sentences.ar: אַף־עַל־פִּי־כֵן הִכְנִיס יָדוֹ לְתוֹךְ אַרְנָקוֹ – וְהוֹצִיא שְׁלֹש מֵאוֹת דִינָרִים.
sentences.en: Even so he put his hand into his purse — and took out three hundred dinars.

sentences.ar: שָׂמַח מְאֹד וְנָתַן דְמֵי הַשְּׁוָרִים וְחָזַר לְבֵיתוֹ וְחָרַשׁ קַרְקְעוֹתָיו.
sentences.en: He rejoiced greatly, paid the price of the oxen, went back home, and plowed his fields.

sentences.ar: הָיְתָה שְׁנַת בְּרָכָה וּמָצָא מֵאָה שְׁעָרִים וְעָשְׁרוֹ נִתְכַּפֵּל.
sentences.en: It was a year of blessing, and he reaped a hundredfold, and his wealth was doubled.

sentences.ar: מִכָּאן שֶׁכָּל אָדָם הָרוֹצֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת שׁוּם דָבָר צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר: אִם יִרְצֶה הַשֵּׁם, שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ מַה יִּהְיֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מִבֹּקֶר עַד עֶרֶב.
sentences.en: From this we learn that anyone who wants to do anything must say "God willing," for he does not know what will happen in this world from morning to evening.

sentences.ar: וְהָיוּ רַבִּים שֶׁאָמְרוּ: אֲנִי אֲנִי אֶעֱשֶׂה, וְלֹא הִסְפִּיקוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת עַד שֶׁנִּתְקַפְּחוּ חַיֵּיהֶם.
sentences.en: And there were many who said, "I, I will do it," and they did not manage to do it before their lives were cut short.

sentences.ar: וְכֵן אָמַר בֶּן סִירָא: מִבֹּקֶר עַד עֶרֶב הָעוֹלָם יֵחָרֵב.
sentences.en: And so Ben Sira said: "From morning to evening the world may be destroyed."

translation: English by Claude — the Hebrew is Project Ben-Yehuda's, verbatim
